gemini.rationale: The transaction involved the purchase of closed store leases, fixtures, and equipment (T4/T5 subset) out of bankruptcy, with the seller retaining all inventory, intellectual property, and goodwill. The buyer did not assume any employees or labor agreements (T6 null), creating a structural gap between the acquired operational assets (T5) and the people who previously ran them (T6). There is no mention of a transitional services agreement to mitigate this gap.

grok.rationale: Per EX-99.1 §1.1(a)–(b), the Assets that crossed were store leases, fixtures/equipment, assigned contracts, and transferable permits/liquor licenses for already-closed stores, while inventory, pharmacy assets, IP/goodwill, software rights, and books/records on chain-wide or division-level operations, policies and plans were expressly excluded—creating a documented T4 retail-asset transfer without accompanying T5 operating processes (gap_45=1). T5 processes themselves did not transfer as a going concern (stores closed; ops records retained by Seller), and EX-99.1 §4.5 states Buyer offered no employment and assumed no labor agreements, so T5 and T6 both ended rather than T5 moving without T6 (gap_56=0); no transitional-services or operating agreement allocating shared substrate is documented.

openai.rationale: The acquired customer-facing store base included leases, fixtures, equipment, signage, point-of-sale hardware, licenses, and assigned contracts, but the closed stores transferred without inventory, pharmacy assets, software rights, intellectual property, goodwill, or chain-wide operational records (EX-99.1 §1.1(a)-(b)); this documents a product-process gap at closing. Operational assets and some vendor agreements crossed, while Buyer had not agreed to employ Seller personnel, assumed no labor agreements, and Seller retained employee records and WARN obligations (EX-99.1 §§1.1(b), 4.5), establishing a process-organization gap. No transitional-services or operating agreement allocating these omitted operational or workforce resources is documented in the slice.
